title: work
content:
1. Trigger
    The app logs an event in Mongo when the user leaves a clinic page without booking. When the app calls GET /alerts/primary_alerts?screen=home, ClinicDropOffAlert.fetch() runs. The user_id comes from the auth token.

  2. Mongo read

  • Collection: VMS app_click_logs.
  • Filter: vetic_user_id = user_id and event_name is cdp_drop_off_event (clinic detail page) or slp_drop_off_event (clinic listing page).
  • It sorts by created_at descending and takes only the latest event.
  • The query itself has no date filter. The age check happens later: a "new" user's event is valid for 15 days, a "repeat" user's for 24 hours.

  1. Checks, in order (any one fails → no card)

  2. Persona: the user must be tagged "new" or "repeat" in IAM.

  3. Drop-off: a drop-off event must exist.

  4. Clinic:

    • cdp: use the event's own clinic.
    • slp: last visited clinic → nearest clinic (by lat/lon) → the logged clinic.

  5. Blue 7: the clinic must not be a Blue 7 clinic.

  6. Discount:

    • Member with an unused free vaccination, at a clinic that offers vaccination: 100% off, and the service becomes Vaccination.
    • Everyone else: the highest discount from service_coupons (status ACTIVE, type NORMAL, matching the clinic, persona and service). No coupon or 0% → no card.

  7. Age: the event must be within the 15-day / 24-hour window.

  8. Upcoming appointment: the user must not already have one.

  9. Next slot: a free PRIMARY slot must exist from today to D+3. None → no card.

  10. Next slot
    It queries Postgres staff_slots_new_logic with:

  • this clinic and service;
  • slot_date from today to today+3;
  • slot_type = 'PRIMARY';
  • not booked (appointment_id IS NULL) and visible;
  • for today, only slots after the current IST time.

It picks the earliest free slot on the earliest day that has one.

  1. Bottom rows
    The card's layout and text come from the Mongo alerts collection (doc named CLINIC_DROP_OFF_INTENT). Its placeholders are filled in:
  • bottom_value_1 = the slot as Today, 3:00 PM / Tomorrow, 3:00 PM / 05 Oct, 3:00 PM.
  • bottom_value_2 = the clinic's short name (e.g. Domlur).
  1. "Continue Booking" CTA
    It opens screen_id: 3 (the booking screen) with:
  • pet_id from the event.
  • clinic_id: the resolved clinic.
  • service_id: the browsed service, or vaccination for a free-vaccination member.
  • date: the day the slot was found, so the booking screen opens on the day the card shows.
  • city_id: the clinic's district_no from the clinic DB.
  • from: empty, because the clinic event doesn't log a source.



PENDING DIAGONSTIC ALERT

  1. Trigger
    A vet adds or recommends lab tests in a pet's EMR during a visit. Later, when the app calls GET /alerts/primary_alerts?screen=home, PendingDiagnosticsAlert.fetch() runs. The user_id comes from the auth token. pet_id comes from the request context if the screen sends one; the home screen usually doesn't.

  2. Mongo reads (all from vetic_vms)

  • EMRs (emr):
    • Filter: customer_details.customer_id = user_id and created_at within the last 60 days (epoch seconds). If a pet_id is given, also pet_details.pet_id = pet_id.
    • Sorted newest EMR first.
    • From each EMR it collects every test in lab_test_and_diagnostics.lab_test_added and lab_test_recommended, along with its lab_test_id (the bom_id), emr_id and the EMR's pet_id.
  • Invoices (invoices):
    • Filter: user_id = user_id, created_at within the last 60 days, and status != cancelled.
    • It builds a map from each EMR to the tests already billed against it (emr_details on each line, or the older single emr_id field).
    • First it grabs all the user's invoices from the last 60 days (not searching, just pulls everything). For every item in every invoice, it reads that item's emr_id and builds a dictionary: emr_id → {bom_ids billed under it}.
    • 2. Now that dictionary is like an index. Given ANY emr_id, you can instantly look up "what got billed under this."
    • Then for each EMR-side test — which already carries its own emr_id (since we read it straight off the EMR doc itself) — code just does:
    • invoiced_by_emr.get(test["emr_id"])
    • Same string, same key. That's the whole jump — not a real "link," just both sides happening to share the same emr_id value, so a plain dict lookup connects them.
  • Catalog (billing_material):
    • Filter: those bom_ids with status = true, app_status = true and bom_type = "Lab".
    • The test name is display_name, or bom_name if that's missing.

  1. Checks, in order (any one fails → no card)

  2. App version: must be 4.5.0 or newer, because older builds don't have the diagnostics booking screen.

  3. Recommendations: at least one lab test must be recommended in the last 60 days.

  4. Not billed yet: a test is dropped if it was already invoiced against the same EMR it was recommended in. Duplicates are merged per (pet, test), so two pets with the same test stay separate.

  5. Visible in the app: only tests in the catalog check above survive. Anything else is dropped rather than shown with a blank name.

  6. One pet per card: the pet with the newest pending recommendation wins. Only that pet's tests go on the card, and other pets' tests wait for their own turn.

  7. Tests left: at least one test must remain after all of this.

  8. Card text
    The layout comes from the Mongo alerts collection (doc named PENDING_DIAGNOSTICS). The code fills in:

  • heading = {pet_name}'s pending lab tests, with pet_name looked up from pet_id.
  • title = the test names:
    • 1 test: CBC
    • 2 tests: CBC & KFT
    • 3 or more: CBC, KFT & 2 more
    • none: Lab tests

There's no slot lookup and no discount. In legacy v4 the fixed copy was subtitle "Recommended by your vet", status "Recommended", and button "Book Now".

  1. "Book Now" CTA
    It opens screen_id: 70 (the diagnostics booking journey) with:
  • pet_id: the winning pet.
  • lab_ids: that pet's pending test ids, so the booking screen opens with them already selected.
  1. Difference from legacy v4
  • Data source: legacy called clinic_org's /lab-test/app/diagnostics/recommended/ over HTTP, forwarding the user's token. The new code reads the same EMR, invoice and catalog data directly from Mongo.
  • Pet: legacy needed a pet_id in the request and returned nothing without one. The new code works without it and picks the pet from the data.
  • Suppression: no rule in ALERT_SUPPRESSION_RULES or PRIMARY_ALERT_CROSS_SUPPRESSION_RULES hides this card.
